extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate/graduate students and contest mathematicians studying algebraic number theory (readers of Evan Chen's 'Napkin')
extracted.subtask_description: Expository textbook/lecture-note material on algebraic number theory topics (discriminant, units, Galois theory, finite fields) including definitions, theorems, examples, and problem prompts. Aimed at learners working through theory and problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminant of a number field (matrix definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: If α1, ..., αn is a Z-basis for K and σ1, ..., σn are the n embeddings of K into C, then the discriminant ∆K is given by det([σi(αj)]_{i,j})^2 (matrix of embeddings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The displayed Vandermonde-like matrix with rows σi(α1),...,σi(αn) defines the discriminant; several equivalent characterizations and properties follow in the text and problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminant of cyclotomic field (Problem 57A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For p an odd rational prime and K = Q(ζ_p) with ζ_p a primitive pth root of unity, show ∆K = (−1)^{(p−1)/2} p^{p−2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit formula is a concrete example; used as an exercise to compute discriminants for cyclotomic fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace representation of ∆K (Problem 57B)
rubrics_metrics.description: If α1,...,αn is a basis for O_K, then ∆K = det([Tr_{K/Q}(α_i α_j)]_{i,j}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an alternative description of the discriminant as the determinant of the trace form matrix; in particular it shows ∆K is an integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Root (polynomial) representation of ∆K (Problem 57C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K is monogenic with O_K = Z[θ] and f is the minimal (monic) polynomial of θ, then ∆K = ∆(f), where ∆(f) is the polynomial discriminant c^{2n-2} Π_{i<j} (z_i − z_j)^2 (z_i roots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a number field is generated by a single element, the field discriminant equals the polynomial discriminant of the minimal polynomial; problem shows how to translate between the two notions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nontriviality of discriminant (Problem 57D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K ≠ Q is a number field then |∆K| > 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple property ruling out trivial discriminant for nontrivial number fields; used to exclude certain degeneracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brill's theorem on sign of discriminant (Problem 57E)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a number field K with signature (r1,r2), ∆K > 0 if and only if r2 is even.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates the sign of the field discriminant to the parity of the number of complex (conjugate) places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stickelberger congruence for discriminant (Problem 57F)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any number field K, ∆K ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A congruence restriction on discriminants; appears as an exercise to prove.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units criterion (invertibility via norm)
rubrics_metrics.description: An algebraic integer α ∈ O_K is a unit (invertible) if and only if its norm N_{K/Q}(α) = ±1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This characterization (cited from Problem 54A) is used to check invertibility and to reason about unit groups; examples (±1, roots of unity, and other explicit units) illustrate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit group structure (Dirichlet's unit theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let µ(O_K) be the roots of unity in K. For K with signature (r1,r2) set s = r1 + r2 − 1. There exist fundamental units u1,...,us such that every unit α ∈ O_K^× can be written uniquely as α = ω · u1^{n1}···us^{ns} for ω ∈ µ(O_K) and n_i ∈ Z. Equivalently O_K^× ≅ Z^{r1+r2−1} × µ(O_K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated without proof and illustrated with examples: Q(i) (only roots of unity), real quadratic fields (rank 1) with explicit fundamental units; computing fundamental units can be hard in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of µ(O_K) (roots of unity)
rubrics_metrics.description: µ(O_K) denotes the finite subgroup of roots of unity contained in K (e.g., µ(Z[i]) = {±1, ±i}, µ(Z[√3]) = {±1}, µ(Z[(1+√−3)/2]) = sixth roots of unity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise to show µ(O_K) is finite and comprises the roots of x^n − 1 for some n; used in the decomposition of unit groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental units (definition and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: A choice of units u1,...,us which serve as generators of the free rank-s part of O_K^× (so every unit is ω · u1^{n1}···us^{ns}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and a small table of fundamental units for some small d are provided; computing them is noted to be computationally hard in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental units from Pell's equation (Theorem 58.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For squarefree d, (a) if d ≡ 2,3 (mod 4) and (x,y) is minimal integer solution to x^2 − d y^2 = ±1 then x + y√d is a fundamental unit; (b) if d ≡ 1 (mod 4) use the minimal half-integer solution (or minimal integer solution to a^2 − d b^2 = ±4) to form the fundamental unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete criterion linking minimal solutions of Pell-type equations to fundamental units in real quadratic fields; 'minimal' can be measured by |y|.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units generate Pell solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Integer solutions to x^2 − d y^2 = ±1 correspond to norms ±1 elements in O_K, and powers of a fundamental unit generate all solutions (up to sign and roots of unity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: K = Q(√5) with fundamental unit (1+√5)/2; powers of this unit produce the infinite family of Pell solutions, patterned by norms ±1 alternating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding (definition) and enumeration (Theorem 59.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An embedding σ : K → C is an injective field homomorphism fixing Q. For a number field K of degree n there are exactly n such embeddings σ1,...,σn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: build K by adjoining generators and count choices per adjoining step; examples illustrate real and complex embeddings and how roots map to conjugates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace and norm via embeddings (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a number field K of degree n with embeddings σ1,...,σn into C, define Tr_{K/Q}(α) = Σ_i σ_i(α) and N_{K/Q}(α) = Π_i σ_i(α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This coincides with earlier algebraic definitions; used heavily in discriminant and unit characterizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separable polynomial / separable extension / perfect field (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A polynomial is separable if it has no repeated roots. A separable extension K/F is one where each element's minimal polynomial over F is separable. A perfect field is one in which every finite extension is separable (e.g., characteristic 0 fields and finite fields).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristic issues (especially characteristic p) can make derivatives zero and give inseparable polynomials; lemma: irreducible polynomials over characteristic zero fields are separable; finite fields are perfect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embeddings for separable extensions (Theorem 59.4.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K/F is a separable extension of degree n and F an algebraic closure, then there are exactly n field homomorphisms K → F fixing F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes the earlier count-of-embeddings theorem beyond Q to any separable base field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphism group Aut(K/F) (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aut(K/F) is the group of field automorphisms σ: K → K which fix F; composition is the group operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Aut(Q(i)/Q) ≅ Z/2Z; Aut(Q(∛2)/Q) is trivial; automorphisms permute Galois conjugates and preserve minimal polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Splitting field (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given p(x) ∈ F[x] with roots α1,...,αn in an algebraic closure, the splitting field is F(α1,...,αn), the smallest field where p splits completely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cautionary examples: adjoining one root of x^3 − 2 does not yield the other roots; splitting fields can have degree up to n! depending on relations among roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois extension criterion and sizing (Theorem 59.5.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite extensions K/F, |Aut(K/F)| divides [K:F], with equality iff K is the splitting field of some separable polynomial over F. When equality holds, K/F is Galois and Aut(K/F) is denoted Gal(K/F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galois extensions are characterized intrinsically by having as many F-automorphisms as the degree; examples: Q(√2)/Q is Galois, Q(∛2)/Q is not; Galois closure adds missing conjugates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental theorem of Galois theory (Theorem 59.6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K/F is Galois with G = Gal(K/F), then (a) subgroups H ⊆ G correspond bijectively (inclusion-reversing) to intermediate fields F ⊆ E ⊆ K via H ↦ K^H; (b) [K : E] = |H| and [E : F] = |G/H|; (c) K/E is Galois with Gal(K/E)=H; (d) E/F is Galois iff H is normal in G, and then Gal(E/F) ≅ G/H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theorem is stated (no full proof) and illustrated with examples (e.g., Klein four example) and exercises; shows tight correspondence between subgroup structure and intermediate fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed field theorem (Theorem 59.8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a field K and subgroup G ≤ Aut(K), [K : K^G] = |G|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in proving the equality case in the Galois criterion and in arguments that build polynomials with coefficients fixed by G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Root closure for irreducible polynomials in Galois extensions (Lemma 59.8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K/F is Galois and p ∈ F[x] is irreducible, then if any root of p lies in K then all roots lie in K and p is separable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct S = {σ(α) | σ ∈ Gal(K/F)} and form the polynomial Π_{β∈S} (x−β) to show coefficients lie in F, so irreducible p must equal that separable product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite field classification (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite field F has order p^n for some prime p and integer n; F has characteristic p; any finite field is a finite extension of F_p; all finite fields of order p^n are isomorphic (denoted F_{p^n}); the extension F/F_p is Galois with Gal(F/F_p) cyclic of order n generated by Frobenius x ↦ x^p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is summarized at the start of Chapter 60 and illustrated by examples (F_p, F_9 ≅ F_3[x]/(x^2+1)). The Frobenius automorphism plays the central role in the Galois group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic of a nonzero field element is prime (Lemma 60.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the characteristic of a field F is nonzero, it must be a prime number p (i.e., the least positive n with n·1_F = 0 is prime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction: if n = ab composite then nonzero additive elements multiply to zero, contradicting field property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite fields have prime power order and are extensions of F_p (Lemma 60.2.2 / 60.2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is finite then its characteristic is a prime p, F contains a copy of F_p, and F is a finite-dimensional vector space over F_p so |F| = p^n for some n. Conversely, if |F| = p^n then F contains an isomorphic copy of F_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use additive group structure and vector-space arguments; alternate arguments by contradiction using Cauchy's theorem are sketched.
